gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured Starlink Mini run: Martin Sauter (wirelessmoves) found a 60 W USB-C power bank left the Mini stuck in a boot loop, while a 100 W, 72 Wh Anker Prime bank ran it for 2 h 45 min and steady draw was about 21 W.
standout_why: ChatGPT drew only on Starlink pages: Help Center a7fe6525 and fba85643 (cited), the USB-C cable article and the Mini accessories PDF. Its answer gives a spec table (100 W PD, '25–40W typical') and a runtime table worked out from an assumed 30 W at 85% efficiency, with no measurement from a named tester. None of those results contains a real powered run, a measured 60 W failure or a measured steady draw. I could not render the Starlink pages myself because they are JavaScript-only, so this comparison uses ChatGPT's answer and the result titles. Its '60W not supported' line is a spec claim; the wirelessmoves boot loop is the first observed test of it.
decides: The measured run backs the 100 W PD rule: a 60 W bank failed and a 100 W bank worked. It also shows real draw is lower than ChatGPT's 30 W assumption: 72 Wh lasted 2.75 h, about 26 W counting the bank's own losses. Our 'hours' column (20–40 W) should be anchored near 21–26 W. On that basis the 288 Wh Elite 30 V2 and 286 Wh RIVER 3 Plus sit near the top of their '6–12 h' range, and every listed station needs a USB-C port rated 100 W or more (all qualify: 100–140 W).
candidates: Anker Prime 20,000 mAh power bank (the bank the testers used)
